description: Ford Motor, founded in 1903, was the second-largest automaker by revenue in the U.S. in 2024. It manufactures cars, trucks, and commercial vehicles, and owns the luxury car brand Lincoln. Ford entered the electric vehicle market in the late 1990s with its Ford Ranger EV and has since expanded its EV lineup to include the F-150 Lightning pickup truck, the Mustang Mach-E SUV, and E-Transit electric commercial van.

rankings.itemDescription:
For the fifth year in a row, Ford is the largest U.S. automaker by sales; it brought in $158 billion in revenue last year.

  • Ford dealt with slowed production as shortages of computer chips and other parts affected its vehicle assembly lines. It still hit some key goals, including producing its 150,000th Mustang Mach-E in November 2022.

  • In March 2023, Ford announced the establishment of a subsidiary known as Latitude AI to develop automated driving systems. Latitude’s engineers are slated to collaborate with a team that previously worked at Argo AI, a joint venture among Ford, Volkswagen, and others that had shut down months prior.

  • Ford reported a $600 million loss in China in 2022, where stiff competition from rivals such as BYD has cut into its performance. In May 2023, Ford announced that it would scale back investments and reduce costs across its Chinese operations.

rankings.title: Fortune 500
rankings.itemDescription: After a difficult, pandemic-scarred 2020 marked by unit shutdowns, supply-chain issues, and a full-year loss in revenue, Ford Motor began slowly but steadily recovering in 2021. Revenue increased by 7.2%, and Ford’s total return to investors was 137.5% for the year. Even as it rebounded, Ford doubled down on an electric-vehicle future. It accelerated development of the Lightning F-150, an electric version of its bestselling pickup truck that analysts expect will be the first major EV pickup to hit the market when deliveries begin this year. The company is planning to invest as much as $20 billion in EV development over the next 10 years, and in March 2022 it announced that it would split into two units: Ford Model e, for EV manufacturing and development, and Ford Blue, for traditional internal combustion engine vehicles. Ford expects 50% of its global sales to come from EVs by 2030.

rankings.title: Fortune Global 500
rankings.itemDescription: Ford’s global business was whacked by the pandemic, which forced plant closures, caused supply-chain backlogs, and reduced demand for new passenger vehicles. As a result, full-year revenues were down 19%, from $156 billion to $127 billion, and net income was negative $1.3 billion. North America and its credit division were Ford’s only profitable units; still, the company would have eked out a small profit overall were it not for a $1.5 billion pension charge. New CEO Jim Farley, who took the wheel at Dearborn in October 2020, will be banking big on the electric F-150 truck, announced in May 2021, to kick-start Ford’s EV program in earnest.

rankings.itemDescription: Despite a $4.4 billion decline in revenues, Ford retains its position as America’s largest carmaker by revenue for a second consecutive year. The perennially strong performance of its F-series trucks is sustaining the company through an awkward transition in its passenger car lineup. In the next year, investors will be keeping an eye on market adoption of its electric Mustang Mach-E as well as the newly reborn Bronco SUV.

rankings.title: Fortune 500
rankings.itemDescription: Despite a $4.4 billion decline in revenues, Ford Motor Co. retains its position as America’s largest carmaker by revenue for a second consecutive year—the first time it has done so in the history of the Fortune 500. The perennially strong performance of its F-series trucks is sustaining the company through an awkward transition in its passenger car lineup. In the next year, we’ll be keeping an eye on market adoption of its electric Mustang Mach-E as well as the soon-to-be-announced rebirth of the Bronco SUV.
